plan.analysis: Only evidence is the constant step, whose triangular autoconvolution gives R=2/3. Smooth bells should beat it: a continuous Gaussian has R=sqrt(1/2)=0.7071, and step sampling can approach that. Bets: (1) explicit Gaussian width scan, (2) free symmetric step optimization seeded by Gaussian to shape tails/plateau beyond any formula, (3) bounded power-law taper of the constant start to test compact/bell geometry. Each compares exact R against the p0001 start and spends the remaining budget refining rather than stopping early.

experiments.hypothesis: A sampled Gaussian f has an almost Gaussian autoconvolution, giving R near 0.7071, clearly above the triangular 2/3.
experiments.change: Set N=2001 and x_i=(i+0.5)/N. For each width s in a log grid from 0.02 to 0.35, build h_i=exp(-0.5*((x_i-0.5)/s)^2), evaluate exact R from L=[0,*np.convolve(h,h),0] using the given formula, and keep the best. Refine s by ternary/golden search around the best, then if time remains repeat with N=4001 and N=8001. Return the best candidate only if its exact R exceeds R(start); otherwise return start.
experiments.prediction: Best R will be about 0.707, and certainly above 0.690, refuting the idea that the constant is near-optimal.

experiments.hypothesis: Free symmetric step heights can adjust the Gaussian-like seed's tails and center profile to raise R beyond any simple parametric family.
experiments.change: Use N=200 symmetric heights. Parameterize by M=ceil(N/2) log-heights z, set h_i=exp(clip(z_i,-20,5)) and mirror h_{N-1-i}=h_i. Objective is -R(h), evaluated exactly via np.convolve. Run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='L-BFGS-B' using finite differences, seeded from (a) the p0001 start resampled to N, and (b) Gaussians with s=0.08,0.12,0.18. Keep the best iterate over all seeds. If time remains, restart N=320 from the best shape. Return the best overall if it beats R(start), else start.
experiments.prediction: The optimized shape will exceed the best Gaussian seed, reaching R roughly 0.71-0.73 and confirming that nonparametric reshaping helps.

experiments.hypothesis: A compact bell made by tapering the constant start may flatten the autoconvolution peak relative to its tails and beat the constant, testing a different geometry from the Gaussian.

plan.analysis: p0005 (0.814817) is the clear best: its f*f has a broad flat top (~24% of knots within 1% of max), and its heights are all positive with max/mean 2.1. Its search is greedy coordinate ascent and it stopped upsampling whenever interpolation immediately lowered the score. I bet on (1) replacing that search with analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B plus forced resolution doubling, (2) revisiting p0003's parametric flat-top branch with a richer nonzero-floor family and global optimization, and (3) adding non-greedy block simulated annealing on p0005 to escape its local optimum.

experiments.hypothesis: p0005's score is limited by greedy coordinate steps and by stopping upsampling when linear interpolation temporarily lowers R. Exact gradients plus forced higher resolution should find a better discretization of the same broad flat-top shape.
experiments.change: Replace p0005's greedy multiplicative coordinate loop with analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B in log-heights. For h compute L=np.convolve(h,h), Lf=[0,*L,0], A=sum(Lf[:-1]**2+Lf[:-1]*Lf[1:]+Lf[1:]**2)/3, B=sum(h)**2, M=Lf.max(), k=argmax(Lf). Define gA=(Lf[:-2]+4*Lf[1:-1]+Lf[2:])/3; dA_i=2*dot(gA[i:i+N], h[:min(N,len(gA)-i)]); dB=2*sum(h); dM_i=2*h[k-1-i] when 0<=k-1-i<N else 0; dS=(dA - (A/(B*M))*(dB*M+B*dM))/(B*M). Optimize v=log(h+1e-12) via scipy.optimize.minimize(jac=True, method='L-BFGS-B', maxiter=2000, ftol=1e-15, gtol=1e-12). After each solve set h=exp(v), h/=h.max(), record best. Then force upsample with scipy.interpolate.PchipInterpolator to twice N (do not gate on immediate score), reset v=log(h+1e-12), and solve again. Repeat until 0.92*budget. Finish with two greedy coordinate sweeps on the best h.
experiments.prediction: Score should exceed p0005's 0.8148, likely reaching 0.820-0.830 as resolution increases.

experiments.hypothesis: p0003's parametric flat-top branch underperformed because it likely forced zero tails and optimized parameters locally. A symmetric nonzero-floor flat-top with global parameter search should capture p0005's all-positive broad shape and may exceed it.
experiments.change: Base p0003. Define a symmetric 4-parameter profile on N=400: x=(arange(N)+0.5)/N; t=abs(2*x-1); h=e+(1-e)*max(0,1-(t/w)**p)**q, with bounds w in [0.2,1.0], p in [0.5,20], q in [0.1,10], e in [0,0.5]. Maximize R by scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on -R(h) with maxiter=40, popsize=15, tol=1e-6, polish=True. Then Nelder-Mead polish at N=1000. Build the best profile at N=4000 and run p0005-style multiplicative coordinate descent (step 0.1 decaying to 1e-5) for all remaining time, keeping the best. This differs from p0003 by allowing a nonzero edge floor e and using global DE over all four parameters.
experiments.prediction: Should beat p0003's 0.8018; if it also exceeds 0.8148, the nonzero-floor flat-top family contains a better shape than p0005.

experiments.hypothesis: p0005's monotone coordinate ascent is stuck in a local optimum. Non-greedy block moves at nonzero temperature can cross small score valleys and find a better basin.
experiments.change: Base p0005. Run simulated annealing on log-heights h (N=200, normalized max=1). At each iteration: with probability 0.7 pick one index and multiply h[i] by exp(N(0,0.15)); with probability 0.3 pick a contiguous block of length L=random integer 5..50 and multiply all its entries by exp(N(0,0.08)). Normalize h/=h.max(). Accept if new R > current R, otherwise accept with probability exp((newR-currentR)/T), where T decreases geometrically from 5e-5 to 1e-8 over the budget. Whenever a new best is found, run two greedy multiplicative coordinate sweeps (step 0.05 then 0.02) from that point, update the best, and continue SA from the polished point. Use time.process_time() and stop at 0.92*budget; return the best h.
experiments.prediction: Should escape p0005's local optimum and give R>0.8148, likely 0.816-0.822.

plan.analysis: p0012's SA is the strongest line, but it is hard-coded to N=200 and relies on local/block multiplicative proposals. I bet the remaining gap is partly discretization, partly lack of coordinated gradient-like moves, and partly proposal geometry. The three experiments all build directly on p0012 and each changes one mechanism: finer resolution, analytic-gradient optimization of a smoothed surrogate, and SA augmented with broad Gaussian-window moves. All keep the full budget and return the best true-score construction found.

experiments.hypothesis: The N=200 step discretization limits how flat the top of f*f can be made; a finer grid should allow sharper tails and a broader near-max plateau, raising R.
experiments.change: Modify p0012 so it does NOT force N=200. Set N=800. If start has fewer steps, upsample it by linear interpolation over normalized index (np.interp(linspace(0,1,N), linspace(0,1,len(start)), start)); do not downsample. Run the same greedy+SA scheme on N=800, but scale the proposal sizes: greedy steps (0.03,0.01); SA single-coordinate lognormal sigma 0.12; block lengths uniform in [10,120]. Keep the temperature schedule T_hi=5e-5 to T_lo=1e-8. Polish only when a new global best is found, and cap polish sweeps so SA continues until near the deadline. Return the best N=800 array.
experiments.prediction: Score rises above 0.8225, likely 0.823-0.826, with a flatter f*f top. If it stalls at or below 0.8216, the 200-step discretization is not the bottleneck.

experiments.hypothesis: SA in 200 dimensions is inefficient; an analytic gradient of a smooth surrogate can move all heights coherently and reach a better local optimum than local multiplicative moves.
experiments.change: Start from p0012 resized to N=200. Optimize x=log(h) with Adam for most of the budget. Compute g=np.convolve(h,h); q=(roll(g,1)+4*g+roll(g,-1))/3 with zero padding; dS/dh=2*np.correlate(q,h,'valid'). Replace max(g) by the p-norm M=m0*(sum((g/m0)**p))**(1/p) with p=40, where m0=g.max(); set dM/dg=(g/m0)**(p-1) * (sum((g/m0)**p))**(1/p-1); dM/dh=2*np.correlate(dM/dg,h,'valid'). Then grad_logR=dS/S - 2/sum(h) - dM/M, and the gradient wrt x is h*grad_logR. Use Adam with lr ~1e-2, renormalize h/=h.max() each step. Every ~200 iterations evaluate the true score; whenever it beats the best, store h and run a short p0012 greedy polish on it. At the end return the best true-score array.
experiments.prediction: The gradient path finds a smoother, flatter-top construction and scores at least 0.8225. If it stalls below p0012, the softmax approximation or non-smooth true max is too damaging.

experiments.hypothesis: p0012's local and contiguous-block moves cannot make coordinated broad shape changes; adding smooth Gaussian-window multiplicative proposals lets the SA reshape whole regions and escape the local optimum.
experiments.change: Keep p0012's greedy sweep, temperature schedule, and score exactly, but replace the SA proposal with: with probability 0.4, pick center c uniform in [0,N-1], width w=N*uniform(0.05,0.5), amplitude a~Normal(0,0.05), and multiply h by exp(a*exp(-0.5*((i-c)/w)**2)); otherwise use p0012's existing single-coordinate or contiguous-block lognormal move. Normalize h by its max after each proposal. Keep polishing whenever a new global best appears, and continue until the deadline.
experiments.prediction: Broad smooth moves find a modest improvement, roughly +0.001 to +0.004 over 0.821574. If there is no gain, p0012's local optimum is already robust to coordinated shape changes.

plan.analysis: p0017 is the best at 0.824342, using SA plus greedy polish at N=200. p0014 shows finer grids are promising but its search was weaker.
